messages.author: aa0912ca07910337
messages.subject: measurementInvariance (using semTools)
parts:
Is there a way to make the measurementInvariance() function in semTools to produce the McDonald's noncentrality index (NCI) in addition to the delta CFI as measure of model fit? I was unsuccessful in finding documentation of the difftest function which seems to do the difference testing (e.g. difftest(res$fit.configural, res$fit.loadings)).

According to Meade, Johnson & Braddy (2008) (doi: 10.1037/0021-9010.93.3.568) their simulation studies suggest the CFI and NCI are the best two indicators to use when evaluating whether MI exists.

Best regards,
Tormod

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance (using semTools)
parts:
difftest is an internal function in measurementInvariance and thus it doesn't have documentation. Currently I don't know of any functions to compute McDonald's NCI with lavaan output. However, it seems like something we could integrate into the moreFitIndices and/or measurmentInvariance function in semTools. I'll add that if you have a function that takes a lavaan object as an argument and returns McDonald's NCI you can use lapply and the results of the measurmentInvariance function to compute fit for each model.Example below using moreFitIndices

HW.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
            textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
            speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
#measurementInvariance returns a list of lavaan objects, one for each model
fitMI <- measurementInvariance(HW.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school")

#use lapply to apply the moreFitIndices function to each model
lapply(fitMI, moreFitIndices)

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance (using semTools)
parts:
It looks like the mfi reported in fitMeasures is the same one referenced above (from McDonald 1989).

To use this with measurementInvariance, the following code would work:

HW.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
            textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
            speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
#measurementInvariance returns a list of lavaan objects, one for each model
fitMI <- measurementInvariance(HW.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school")

#use lapply to apply the fitMeasures function to each model and return mfi
lapply(fitMI, fitMeasures, "mfi")

McDonald, R.P. (1989). An Index of Goodness-of-Fit Based on Noncentrality. Journal of Classi -
cation, 6, 97-103.
